headline: Amazon refreshes Kindle with aluminum shells and faster speeds, starting at $150
summary: The new Kindle lineup features aluminum variants, flush displays, and a new $35 page-turner accessory, with prices starting at $150.
details: Amazon has announced a significant refresh for its entire Kindle e-reader lineup, introducing aluminum shells across all models for the first time. The basic Kindle and Paperwhite receive the most substantial upgrades, including faster processors and flush displays, aiming to compete with the growing market of smaller e-readers.

The updated basic Kindle now boasts a processor that opens books 30% faster and features a new screen that sits flush with the chassis, improving touch interaction at the display's edges. It's available today in Ube purple and Graphite, starting at $150 for the ad-supported version and $170 for ad-free.

For a more premium feel, the Kindle Aluminum variant is priced at $190 and comes in Alpine Sky Aluminum or Seaglass Green Aluminum, with no ads. The Paperwhite and Paperwhite Signature also receive flush displays and waterproofing. The Signature model includes an adaptive front light and 32GB of storage, with its aluminum version costing $250.

The Colorsoft, Amazon's most expensive small e-reader, also gets a flush display. Its Signature aluminum version, priced at $320, includes an automatically adjusting front light and a double-tap feature to turn pages. The Paperwhite and Colorsoft models are set to release on October 28.

Complementing the new Kindles, Amazon has launched the Kindle Click, a $35 remote accessory designed for turning pages. This accessory is compatible with any Kindle from 2024 onwards and is particularly useful for readers who don't typically hold their device while reading.

Additionally, all three Kindle models are available in Kids versions with artist-designed covers and include 12 months of Amazon Kids+ for free access to a library of books and audiobooks. These Kids editions range in price from $180 to $300.

headline_marked: HP's [[OmniBook 5 14]] launches with OLED, starting at $699.99
headline: HP's OmniBook 5 14 launches with OLED, starting at $699.99
summary: HP's new laptop boasts an OLED display across all configurations and a thinner, lighter design than Apple's MacBook Neo, starting at $699.99.
details: HP has unveiled the OmniBook 5 14, a new laptop designed to compete with Apple's MacBook Neo. It starts at $699.99 and features an Intel Core 5 315 "Wildcat Lake" processor, 8GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD. The laptop is available in four color options: silver, pink, blue, and green.

A key differentiator for the OmniBook 5 14 is its standard inclusion of an OLED display on all models. While the base configuration offers a 1920 x 1200 resolution with 300 nits of brightness, a higher-resolution 2560 x 1600 OLED panel with 400 nits will be available in March 2027.

The OmniBook 5 14 emphasizes portability, measuring just 0.46 inches thin and weighing 2.56 pounds, making it slightly lighter and thinner than the MacBook Neo. It includes a 1080p webcam, dual speakers, HDMI, a 3.5mm audio jack, and two 10Gbps USB-C ports.

Higher-end configurations can be equipped with up to a Core 7 350 chip, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. HP expects the Wildcat Lake chips to provide good battery life, though real-world performance will be tested upon release.

Alongside the OmniBook 5 14, HP also announced the ProBook 4 G2iS, its thinnest business notebook at 0.47 inches. It will also feature Intel Wildcat Lake chips, 8GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD, launching in December with pricing yet to be announced.
